syllabusTopics: Biomolecules: Introduction and functions of carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, minerals, enzymes and water
Cell: Introduction of cell, concepts of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells

Detail structure of eukaryotic cells: cell wall, cell membrane, mitochondria, plastids, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi bodies, lysosomes, ribosomes, nucleus, chromosomes, cilia, flagella and cell inclusions
Cell division: Concept of cell cycle, types of cell division (amitosis, mitosis and meiosis) and significances

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Energy flows through ecosystems but matter cycles continuously.
Ecological succession describes how communities change over time after disturbance.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A keystone predator (e.g., sea otters) maintains balanced predator-prey dynamics.  ·  Primary succession begins on bare rock or volcanic ash; secondary succession follows disturbances like fire or flooding.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Ecosystem services include pollination, water purification, and climate regulation.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Energy flow: energy transfers through trophic levels (producers → herbivores → carnivores)  ·  Biomass: total mass of living organisms in an ecosystem

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Basic Ecological Concepts  ·  - Ecosystem: a community of living organisms interacting with their physical environment

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Food web = complex network of feeding relationships.  ·  Carrying capacity = max population sustainable by the environment.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Define carrying capacity and give an example.  ·  How do keystone species influence ecosystem structure?

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Distinguish between biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) factors.  ·  Understand the difference between population density and carrying capacity.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Carrying capacity: maximum population size an environment can sustain  ·  Succession: gradual change in species composition over time (primary/secondary succession)

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Food chains and food webs illustrate energy transfer and nutrient cycling.  ·  Competition, predation, and mutualism shape species interactions.  ·  Ecosystems can be classified by location (terrestrial, aquatic, marine) or by productivity level.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Explain primary vs secondary ecological succession.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Learn about ecological succession stages (primary vs secondary).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: - Niche: the role and position of a species within its environment  ·  - Population: all individuals of a species in a given area  ·  - Community: group of interacting populations

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Keystone species have disproportionately large effects on ecosystem structure.  ·  Keystone species = has large impact relative to abundance.
